clue.text: Cheating types can crush a gal's spirit

indicators.note: to crush something is to squash it out of shape, so these letters are pressed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the S of the possessive counting as a letter here

explanation.surface: Bullying people can break a young woman's spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crush' looks like a verb about morale, but it signals an anagram of A GAL'S SPIRIT.
explanation.definitionFit: People who pass off others' writing as their own are cheats of a literary kind.

clue.text: Compare man making revolution with king captured

indicators.note: the king is taken prisoner inside the other piece
turning right round, so the man's name is read backwards

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Someone compares a revolutionary to a man who seized a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making revolution' turns NEIL into LIEN, and 'captured' puts K inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To liken one thing to another is to draw a comparison between them; both verbs.

clue.text: Maybe bridge crosses land that's wet and yellow

indicators.note: one piece goes across the other, so the wet land sits inside the card game

parts.note: bridge is an example of a game, hence 'Maybe'
a bog is soft wet ground

explanation.surface: A bridge spans boggy ground that is damp and yellowish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' reads as a structure over a marsh, but it is the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamboge is a deep yellow pigment from tree resin, and the name of that colour.

clue.text: English saint unknown in an American capital

parts.note: St Alban is honoured as the first British martyr

explanation.surface: An English holy man of uncertain identity turns up in a US state capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Albany is the capital city of New York State.

clue.text: Suffered inside having taken acidic milk, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the milk word is spoken, giving a spelling that sounds the same

parts.note: curd is milk soured and thickened by acid

explanation.surface: Someone felt unwell inside after drinking sour milk, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having taken' just joins IN to the sounded piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss or cost is to suffer it, past tense for past tense.

clue.text: Travel in opposite directions — feature outwardly noticeable

indicators.note: the compass points are placed inside the feature word

parts.note: a trait is a distinguishing characteristic you can see
north and south, N and S, point opposite ways

explanation.surface: Moving both ways at once leaves a mark anyone could see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outwardly' looks like a container signal, but it belongs to the description of a trait; 'in' does the placing.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is the act of travelling or passing across from one place to another.

clue.text: Exposer of bad things — one telling us the game's over?

definitions.meaning: a person who reveals wrongdoing inside an organisation

definitions.text: one telling us the game's over?
definitions.meaning: a referee blows a whistle to end a match

explanation.definitionFit: An informer on corporate misconduct, or literally the official who blows the final whistle.

clue.text: The Spanish red wine being handed around — coming from this?

definitions.text: The Spanish red wine being handed around — coming from this?

indicators.note: the wine is passed round the Spanish article, so it encloses it

explanation.surface: Spanish red is passed round the table, perhaps fetched from a wine cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also hints at the answer: wine being handed round may well come from this cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellaret is a sideboard or cabinet for holding bottles of wine.

clue.text: Women wearing the trousers may not be seen as such!

definitions.text: Women wearing the trousers may not be seen as such!

parts.words: Women wearing the trousers may not be seen as such!
parts.note: women in trousers are not thought of as dressing like the other sex, though literally they wear men's clothes

explanation.surface: Women who dominate the home are not necessarily seen as cross-dressers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing the trousers' is the idiom for being in charge, but here it is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: People who wear clothes associated with the opposite sex.

clue.text: Rubbish with nasty smell all right for burying

indicators.note: the smell word buries the other piece inside itself

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: Garbage that stinks is fine to bury.
explanation.definitionFit: Hokum is nonsense or bunkum, a synonym of rubbish in the sense of silly talk.

clue.text: Robber can be cruel, horrible, stealing pounds

indicators.note: something horrible is distorted, so these letters are rearranged
pounds are taken away from the jumble

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A thief can be cruel and nasty when taking money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible' rearranges CAN BE CRUEL, and 'stealing pounds' takes its L away, leaving the nine letters of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A buccaneer is a pirate, which is a robber on the high seas.

clue.text: Dawn's sort of drink? Quite the opposite

definitions.text: Dawn's sort of drink? Quite the opposite

parts.words: Dawn's sort of drink? Quite the opposite
parts.note: the drink is taken not at sunrise but at sunset

explanation.surface: Someone asks if this is a morning tipple, and is told it is the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dawn' looks like a woman's name, but it is daybreak; the opposite time is dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcoholic drink taken around sunset, originally in colonial Africa.

clue.text: Sarah is back as Paul's companion

indicators.note: both pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: Sal is a short form of Sarah

explanation.surface: Sarah has returned to accompany Paul.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul here is St Paul; his companion on missionary journeys in Acts is named in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Acts of the Apostles, Silas travels with Paul on his second missionary journey.

clue.text: Provide new kit for returning criminal

indicators.note: going back, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: to retool is to re-equip with new tools

explanation.surface: Someone supplies fresh gear to a reoffending crook.
explanation.definitionFit: A looter is a thief who plunders during disorder, so a type of criminal.

clue.text: Seaman departed having grabbed copper for kiss

indicators.note: the seaman and departed pieces seize the copper between them

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A sailor who has died had grabbed a policeman to kiss him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To osculate is a formal or jocular word for to kiss.

clue.text: Like goods sent back to base to be mended?

definitions.text: Like goods sent back to base
definitions.meaning: goods put back in the store are stored again
repaired, brought back to good condition

explanation.definitionFit: Read as re-stored it means put into storage again; as one word, repaired.

clue.text: French former footballer on a lake in Swiss region

parts.note: Eric Cantona is a French former Manchester United striker
L is a map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A retired French football star relaxes beside a lake in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: Switzerland is divided into cantons, and the adjective describes things relating to one.

clue.text: Support a terrible fellow audibly in card game

indicators.note: signals that the phrase is spoken, giving a spelling that sounds the same

parts.note: back a rat: back means support, a rat is a nasty fellow

explanation.surface: Someone loudly backs a scoundrel at the card table.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccarat is a casino gambling game played with cards.

clue.text: What can be awfully bad on old fellows?

definitions.text: What can be awfully bad on old fellows?

indicators.note: done badly, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A question about what looks terrible on elderly men.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a paunch can look bad on old men.
explanation.definitionFit: The belly region, which in older men may sag or bulge unflatteringly.

clue.text: Something botanical seen in track in Home Counties

indicators.note: the track is placed inside the region

parts.note: the counties around London, in South East England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: A plant feature is spotted on a footpath near London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London, in the South East (SE).
explanation.definitionFit: A spathe is a large bract enclosing a flower cluster, as on an arum lily.

clue.text: Soldier cuts short in broadcast? It doesn't seem to make sense

definitions.text: It doesn't seem to make sense

indicators.note: on air, so the word is heard and replaced by one sounding alike

parts.note: docks means cuts short, as a tail

explanation.surface: A soldier trims an on-air piece, which seems senseless.
explanation.definitionFit: A paradox is a statement that appears self-contradictory or absurd.

clue.text: Hypocritical language very big in some poetical pieces

parts.note: OS is outsize, a clothing size

explanation.surface: Very grand insincere phrasing appears in some verses.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantos are the main divisions of a long poem.

clue.text: Worked with head covered (it could get greasy)

indicators.note: the first letter is hidden from view, so it drops out

explanation.surface: Someone laboured in a cap, getting messy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something oiled has been coated with lubricant, so it is slick and greasy.

clue.text: Eats baker prepared — for times like these?

indicators.note: made ready, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Snacks the baker made, suited to rest periods.
explanation.definitionFit: Short pauses at work for a cuppa, which is when one eats the baker's goods.

clue.text: Commercial promotion by head of marketing in business organisation

indicators.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An advert from the marketing chief within a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Admin, short for administration, is the organising side of running a business.

clue.text: Cafe in Paris is a pit — it I avoided!

indicators.note: the letter is kept out of the word

explanation.surface: A Parisian café is a dump, so I stayed away.
explanation.definitionFit: An estaminet is a small French café or bar.

clue.text: Object when strange editor goes the wrong way

indicators.note: travelling backwards, so the pieces are read in reverse

explanation.surface: Someone protests when an odd editor heads off in the wrong direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise an objection, verb for verb.

clue.text: Old people struggling along with boys receiving a kiss

indicators.note: in difficulty, so the letters are thrown about
the boys take in the other piece

parts.note: X is a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Elderly folk battle along with lads getting a peck.
explanation.definitionFit: The Germanic peoples who settled England after the Romans, a historic people.
